hero.name: Ayenew Shiferaw
hero.description: UX/UI designer focused on creating simple, user-centered digital experiences through research, wireframing, and prototyping.

about: I'm Ayenew Shiferaw, a UX/UI designer with a multidisciplinary foundation in architecture, mobile app design, and human centered problem solving. I design with intention: every screen, flow, and interaction is shaped by clarity, structure, and empathy.

My journey began in architecture, where I learned how systems, space, and human behavior intersect. Today, I bring that same analytical mindset into digital design creating intuitive interfaces, scalable design systems, and thoughtful user experiences for real-world products. I've designed for fintech, travel, and education platforms, including mobile apps with complex user flows and transaction heavy interactions. Whether I'm conducting research, mapping journeys, wireframing, or prototyping in Figma, I focus on making products feel effortless and meaningful for the people who use them.

I thrive in collaborative, fast-moving environments and love transforming ideas into clean, functional, and visually engaging solutions. My goal is simple: design experiences that solve problems, reduce friction, and make life easier for users.

cases.title: Hid-Go Flight Booking App
cases.cardDesc: A redesigned booking flow that simplifies flight search and cuts task completion time for travelers.
cases.subtitle: A redesigned mobile booking flow for domestic flights in Ethiopia — search, compare, and book in a few clear steps.

shots.alt: Hid-Go fare and seat selection screen

cases.overview: Hid-Go needed a mobile booking experience that could stand up to established travel apps. The existing flow asked too much of users too early, and the search-to-booking path had too many steps for what should be a quick task on a small screen.

process.intro: A standard double-diamond approach, scaled for a solo practice project: understand the problem and the traveler, define what actually matters, explore options, design the screens, then test the flow against the personas below.

cases.problem: Travelers were dropping off midway through booking. Flight search results were dense and hard to scan, filters were buried, and the checkout flow mixed low-priority details in with the steps that actually mattered — picking a flight and paying. On mobile, this meant a lot of scrolling, backtracking, and abandoned sessions.

personas.intro: Before sketching any screens, I defined four traveler personas based on common patterns in how people search for and book domestic flights. Each one pushed different priorities into the design.

items.name: The Frequent Flyer
items.summary: Books often, wants speed and consistency.

items.name: The Budget Hunter
items.summary: Price-driven, compares every option before paying.

items.name: The Family Planner
items.summary: Books for several people at once.
frustrations: Re-entering the same details per passenger

items.name: The First-Time Flyer
items.summary: Unfamiliar with booking and airport terms.
goals: Know exactly what to do on travel day

competitive.intro: A quick feature comparison against the two categories of apps travelers already use, to find where Hid-Go could genuinely be faster or clearer rather than just different.

cases.insight: Across all four personas, the common thread was trust in the price shown. Whether someone was chasing the cheapest fare or just wanted to get through checkout without surprises, the fare tiers needed to be transparent and the total needed to stop changing after it was first shown. That single insight drove the fare and payment screens more than anything else.

ia.intro: The app is organized around four tabs, with the booking flow itself living as a linear path from search to confirmation.

flow.title: User flow — booking a flight
flow.intro: The core path a traveler follows from opening the app to holding a confirmed booking, shown on the real screens.

cases.solution: The redesigned flow simplifies flight search into a cleaner, scannable results list, surfaces filters that travelers actually use, and streamlines checkout into a shorter, clearer sequence. Fare tiers and seat selection live on one screen so the price never shifts after that point, and the confirmation screen doubles as a boarding-pass-style record of the trip.

style.intro: Hid-Go's real design tokens — the same colors, type, and components used in the working prototype.
style.sampleBody: A redesigned booking flow that simplifies flight search and cuts task completion time for travelers.

cases.outcome: The redesign delivered a noticeably improved mobile experience with faster task completion through the booking flow, giving Hid-Go a foundation that's easier to extend as the product grows.

cases.title: Guxo Bus Booking App
cases.cardDesc: A sibling app to Hid-Go, retheming the same booking patterns for intercity bus travel under a fictional operator brand.
cases.subtitle: A sibling app to Hid-Go, extending the same booking patterns to intercity bus travel in Ethiopia.

shots.alt: Guxo fare and seat selection screen

cases.overview: Once Hid-Go's booking flow was working well, the natural next step was testing whether that same foundation could carry a different mode of travel. Guxo takes the flight-booking patterns from Hid-Go and rebuilds them for intercity bus travel, under its own visual identity and a fictional operator, "Guxo Line."

process.intro: The same double-diamond approach as Hid-Go, run a second time to make sure the patterns held up for a genuinely different mode of travel rather than just a reskin.

cases.problem: A straight reskin wouldn't hold up. Bus travel has a different seat layout (2+2, not 3+3), a different route network built around major Ethiopian cities rather than airports, and different fare tiers that needed to make sense for a multi-hour road trip rather than a flight. It also needed to look and feel like its own product, not "Hid-Go in green." And unlike flights, most riders were booking through a walk-up counter or a phone call to an agent — not an app at all.

personas.intro: Bus travelers in Ethiopia skew broader than flyers — more price-sensitive, more likely booking in person today. I defined four rider personas to keep the redesign honest about that gap.

items.name: The Daily Commuter
items.summary: Rides the same route often, wants speed.
frustrations: No way to check seats before arriving
goals: Book a seat in minutes from a phone

items.name: The Budget Traveler
frustrations: Unclear what Comfort vs. Standard includes

items.name: The Family Traveler
items.summary: Books several seats for a multi-hour trip.

items.name: The First-Time Rider
frustrations: Not knowing which station to use

competitive.intro: Guxo isn't competing with other apps so much as with how bus tickets are actually bought today in Ethiopia.

cases.insight: The personas and the competitive picture pointed to the same gap: riders don't currently get to see a seat before they own it. Whether it's a commuter checking availability or a family trying to sit together, being able to see and pick real seats — not just "a ticket" — was the one thing no existing option offered.

ia.intro: Rebuilt from Hid-Go's structure, with the same four-tab shape adapted to bus travel.

flow.title: User flow — booking a bus
flow.intro: The same core path as Hid-Go, adapted to a 2+2 cabin and Guxo's own fare tiers, shown on the real screens.

cases.solution: The result is a fully separate booking flow with its own brand: a fictional operator and an original bus glyph, rather than any real carrier's name or logo, plus an original illustrated hero scene in place of a stock photo. The seat map was rebuilt from 3+3 to a genuine 2+2 layout, fare tiers were renamed and re-priced for a road trip (Standard, Comfort, VIP), and every "flight" concept in the original code was traced through and replaced with its bus equivalent, down to the icon set and copy.

style.intro: Guxo's real design tokens — a teal-and-gold system built to feel distinct from Hid-Go's blue, even while sharing its structure.
style.sampleBody: A sibling app to Hid-Go, retheming the same booking patterns for intercity bus travel under a fictional operator brand.

cases.outcome: Guxo proved the underlying system could extend to a new transportation mode without rebuilding from scratch, and set the pattern for how future apps in this lineup will share the same foundation while still feeling distinct.

cases.title: Modern Hotel Booking App
cases.cardDesc: A ground-up hotel booking app covering search, booking, and edge cases like failed payments and empty states.
cases.subtitle: A ground-up hotel booking app aiming for quality comparable to Booking.com, Airbnb, and Expedia, with its own visual identity and UX.
